name: violin-jab-music-box
idea: Built straight from Kai's recipe: a voice, a jab, then a small foreboding pattern. The lad is a hoarse, shouting lad in his early twenties, half-laughing and slurring, delivering his line like he's yelling it across a taxi rank. A single violent solo violin stab lands right after 'gets home fine', then the strings drop to a tiny out-of-tune music-box figure that loops like a clock. The masked figure is a calm, older woman's voice, low and kind and immovable, like a mum who has waited up; she says 'There's only one.' over the music box alone. End on a soft, filmic car horn swallowed by a reverb tail, no drums anywhere.

name: garage-pulse-cut-dead
idea: A UK garage / 2-step night-out track playing as if from a club door, muffled, with the lad as a cocky young MC-type speaking (not rapping) his line over the skippy beat, giddy and too loud. As the screen splits, the beat stutters, chops and double-tracks into glitchy copies of itself. Everything cuts dead to silence for the masked figure: a very deep, slow bass-baritone man, dry and close, one sentence with no music under it. Then one low sub boom and a single taxi horn tuned to the track's key as the final hit. The idea is the party literally being switched off.

name: lab-theremin-documentary
idea: The masked figure is a lab scientist, so the music is retro science-lab: theremin, oscillator bleeps, a ticking Geiger-counter rhythm and a glassy synth arpeggio that multiplies and detunes as the versions split. The lad is a softer, sleepy, mumbling drunk, intimate and close-mic, almost confiding the line to himself. The masked figure is a crisp, precise middle-aged male documentary-narrator voice, like a nature presenter describing a specimen. The arpeggio collapses back into one sustained pure sine tone on 'only one', then a door thunk and a warm, distant horn under a fading hum.

name: terrace-chant-collapse
idea: The lad's line arrives as a half-sung, half-shouted football-terrace chant by a gang of drunk lads in unison, as if all the infinite versions of him are chanting together, with a scrappy brass band behind them. On the split, the chant fractures into overlapping out-of-time copies. The masked figure is a flat, deadpan young woman, bored and unimpressed, speaking 'There's only one.' and the brass band stops on a tape-stop. Close with a cheeky single trombone slide down and a short, polite taxi beep, funny rather than solemn.

name: vocoder-trailer-braam
idea: Hybrid movie-trailer sound design: rising Shepard-tone riser, ticking clock, heavy braam brass hits. The lad is a fast, breathless, nervous-giggly teenager rattling off his line. The masked figure is the superintelligence itself: a pitched-down, vocoded, slightly robotic voice that sounds enormous and certain, landing 'There's only one.' on a huge low impact with everything else sucked out. The final two seconds are a trailer title-card hit layered with a car horn and headlights-swoosh whoosh, cinematic not annoying.

name: choir-of-yous-to-one
idea: Rainy-city night ambience (wet tyres, distant sirens, a lone saxophone noodling from a bar) under a lad who croons his line out of tune, a sentimental, melancholy drunk singer half-singing to himself. As the versions split, his voice multiplies into a whispering many-voiced choir of himself, layered and stereo-spread and slightly out of sync. The masked figure is a single quiet boy treble-voiced child speaking very plainly, 'There's only one.', and the choir and saxophone collapse into one low piano note in unison. End on rain, a taxi door, and one gentle low horn.
